{{nihongo|'''Tatsumi Shrine Osaka'''|巽神社 (大阪市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

===History===
On April 27, {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} (Meiji 40), the Hachiman Shrine (enshrining Emperor Ōjin) that had been located within {{ill|Tatsumi|Q11479954|qid=Q11479954|lt=Tatsumi Village}} of {{ill|Nakakawachi district|Q11366394|qid=Q11366394}} (formerly {{ill|Shibukawa district|Q11561609|qid=Q11561609}}) was merged with five shrines in the village (the Yokono Shrine in Ōaza Daichi, Aza Inji (a Shikinaisha, enshrining Inshiki-iri-hiko no Mikoto); the Tenjin Grove in Ōaza Ikaga, Aza Ikaga; the Amateru Kōdaijin Shrine in Ōaza Nishiashiro, Aza Yoshinouchi; the Kumano Shrine in Ōaza Yagara, Aza Miyanomae; and the Tenjin Grove in Ōaza Shijō, Aza Yamagōji) through {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=consolidation}}, and was renamed Tatsumi Shrine after the village name.

===Shikinaisha and Yokono Shrine===
About one kilometer northeast of the current location, at Tatsumi-Nishi 3-chome 9 in Ikuno Ward, there is a “Site of Yokono Shrine.” It was formerly a small shrine on a pond called “Inji-no-miya,” but on February 18, {{ill|1731|Q6963|qid=Q6963}} (Kyōhō 16), it was identified as the Shikinaisha Yokono Shrine and renamed accordingly, with its enshrined deity designated as Inshiki-iri-hiko no Mikoto, the second imperial prince of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850}}. The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}} records that the Yokono embankment was constructed in the 13th year of Emperor Nintoku’s reign, and the shrine is believed to have served as the guardian deity of this embankment.
